### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`  _(via evaluateRule (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via /sharing/rules/:idOrName/evaluate (route, bridged from symbol evaluateRule — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via evaluateValidationRules (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 157ebd008b07d0683ee1762d6c858f4ad766618e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f646083565d6dc757a6f67ac3a112897d1074f5f` — the merge of head `2e42d14e43a2c36103e4857a3118b06141e73a63` into base `157ebd008b07d0683ee1762d6c858f4ad766618e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f646083565d6dc757a6f67ac3a112897d1074f5f && git checkout f646083565d6dc757a6f67ac3a112897d1074f5f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 157ebd008b07d0683ee1762d6c858f4ad766618e 2e42d14e43a2c36103e4857a3118b06141e73a63 && git checkout -B drift-repro 157ebd008b07d0683ee1762d6c858f4ad766618e && git merge --no-ff 2e42d14e43a2c36103e4857a3118b06141e73a63

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 157ebd008b07d0683ee1762d6c858f4ad766618e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 157ebd008b07d0683ee1762d6c858f4ad766618e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `2e42d14e43`
Local-runs: none

Scope: the net diff against the merge base (4 files, +289/−12):
- `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`;
- the new `rule-unevaluable-advisory-log.test.ts`, and one engine-level pin added to `advisory-write-answer.test.ts`;
- the changeset.

Read with them:
- the card #24782 with the claim 6307306950 and the dispatch 6307346629;
- the dev's `os-dev-report` 6308216242, read as claims;
- the PR body;
- `records-forms.validation-rule-type-matrix` on `main`: acceptance[5], its `verify`, and knownGaps[1].

### ① Derived judgments

- **The verb is now decided after severity: right.**
  - `RuleContext` gains `advisory`. The loop in `evaluateValidationRules` sets it per rule from the top-level rule's `severity` (`{ ...ctx, advisory: severity !== 'error' }`). A `conditional`'s branch inherits it through `evaluateRule(branch, ctx)`, so the outer rule's severity governs, as it already did for blocking.
  - `failClosedLogger(ctx)` hands the evaluators the write's logger for an `error` rule and none for an advisory one.
  - It sits at the three places that wrote the fail-closed sentence before severity was known: `checkPredicate` (its own line and its `traversalScopeRefusal`), and `checkConditional`'s `when` line and its traversal refusal.
  - `checkPredicate`'s logger feeds nothing but those two lines, so nothing else goes quiet for an advisory rule.
  - The one RuleContext literal sets `advisory: false`, and the interface makes the member required, so no context can miss it.
- **One advisory line, worded as what happened: right.**
  - For an unevaluable advisory rule, the loop reports `unevaluableAdvisoryMessage` through the same two outlets as before: the #13889 seed / boot fold, or the per-write `warn`.
  - The line reads `the rule could not be evaluated (FAULT) — write proceeded: the rule is advisory, so it was not applied to this write`. It names `its branch 'X'` when the fault is a `conditional`'s branch.
  - `FAULT` is `constraint.fault`, the summary `describeCelFault` builds, so no "write rejected" travels with it. The delete-cleanup refusal (`referentialClearRefusal`) spreads the original `constraint`, so it is still `unevaluable` and takes the same path.
- **Nothing that blocks or answers moves.**
  - The violation objects, the `ValidationError` and its 400 body, which rules block, and the #22726 advisory events are all untouched. The `!unevaluable` guard on `advisories.push` is the same predicate, renamed.
  - The `error` path keeps its one fail-closed line. Its refusal message still ends `— write rejected.`.
  - The field-level slots (`requiredWhen`, `readonlyWhen`, option `visibleWhen`) are not reached by this change.
- **The pins have teeth.**
  - Eight unit pins cover `warning` and `info` script conditions, a `conditional`'s `when`, the traversal refusal and the seed fold. Each asserts one line with the rule, the severity, the fault and `write proceeded`, and neither rejection phrase.
  - Three `error` controls assert the refusal and its one fail-closed line.
  - One engine-level pin asserts that `protocol.createData` stores the row, answers no `warnings`, and logs one line.
  - In the ablation, the 6 advisory pins go red and the 3 controls stay green. The blob was restored equal to `HEAD`.
  - Not pinned: the `its branch 'X'` wording of an unevaluable `conditional` branch. It is the same seam and a one-line choice. It is noted, not owed.
- **The checklist:**
  - acceptance[5] scores the absence of the rejection wording, "not whichever replacement sentence #24782 picks", so no clause changes here;
  - knownGaps[1] says "When #24782's fix merges, re-run the clause and drop this line". Its trigger is after the merge, so the PR rightly leaves it. The seat points `domain:devx` to it at landing.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` for `@objectstack/objectql`: right for log text, with no response, status, code, outcome or export moving.
- The changeset and the PR body carry the claim's `Clause-②: no (log text only: …)` line verbatim, at a line start.
- No new export: `failClosedLogger` and `unevaluableAdvisoryMessage` are module-local, and `RuleContext` is an unexported interface.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Cross-lane:** none. No file outside `packages/objectql` and `.changeset/` moved, and no existing pin turned red.
- **Disjoint from #24822** (`domain:services` seat 2's claim in the same file). The hunks sit at the `RuleContext` interface, `evaluateValidationRules`, `evaluateRule`'s `script` / `cross_field` arm and `checkConditional`, none of them in the static-`readonly` strip. `git merge-tree --write-tree` against today's `origin/main` (`662183604c`) is clean.
- **Deviations, all accepted:**
  - no pin moved;
  - the checklist's knownGaps line is left to `domain:devx`;
  - the model-free commit trailers;
  - the PR subscription not taken by the dev; the seat holds it;
  - the first build attempt's flag-forwarding error, re-run clean.
- **Open question:** A, as the dev settled it. The loop words the line once, after severity, in the per-write line's existing shape.
- **CI on `2e42d14e43`:** 4 of 40 check-runs still running at this read. The ACCEPT waits for green.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24782-advisory-unevaluable-log`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`

**VERDICT: PASS**
